title: Lift: Five Practices Great Managers Do Consistently: Raise Performance and Morale - See Your Employees Thrive
author: Ryan W. Leak
target_audience: Anyone seeking to improve their management effectiveness or workplace culture
primary_purpose: To provide managers with actionable, research-backed practices that elevate team performance and morale, helping employees thrive and organizational goals to be achieved more effectively.

structure_format.narrative_style: Conversational, practical, and motivational, blending stories, research findings, and actionable advice
structure_format.organization: Divided into five main sections, each outlining and detailing one core management practice; includes case studies, self-assessment questions, and implementation tips

key_concepts_lessons: Consistently great managers follow five key practices that distinguish them from average managers.
Elevating others—‘lifting’—is at the heart of impactful leadership.
Listening deeply to employees increases trust, engagement, and innovation.
Clear feedback, recognition of strengths, and support through challenges improve performance and satisfaction.
Great managers create opportunities for employee growth and ownership.
Consistency and authenticity in management lead to lasting positive outcomes for teams.
notable_features: Five-practice framework that is easy to remember and implement
Emphasis on both quantitative performance and qualitative morale
Focuses on building sustainable management habits, not one-off techniques
Relevant for both new and experienced leaders
cultural_historical_context: Released in a time of major workplace transformation post-pandemic, the book responds to increased attention on employee well-being, remote management challenges, and renewed interest in morale as a driver of productivity.
reception_impact: Praised for its relatable style and actionable strategies
Adopted by organizations aiming to improve management culture
Highlighted by reviewers as a fresh, much-needed perspective for modern leaders
Seen as accessible for managers at various career stages
comparable_titles: The Making of a Manager by Julie Zhuo
Leaders Eat Last by Simon Sinek
